newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa rand/bonds closing report.

text.p: A late flurry of dollar sales by local exporters and offshore players on Tuesday helped the rand add more than half-a-cent to its one cent gain overnight.
At the 1400 GMT local finish the rand was pegged at 4.4165/4195 against the dollar from 4.4240/4270 overnight.
A trader said that after a generally quiet day characterised by good two-way exporter and importer interest, New York-based players sold dollars into the market.
They said the selling stemmed from the fact that they were loathe to go into the upcoming Easter weekend long dollars because of the high carry costs.
Another trader said local mining houses had also sold dollars late in the afternoon for the same reason.
"Quite a few mining houses put in dollars at end of day. It was quiet all day until about (1245 GMT) and they came in and sold...It's month-end so they had to clear positions," he said.
Dealers said the currency's progress lower was hampered by the fact that importers were also looking to cover their month-end commitments.
Similar demand for dollars was expected to surface on Wednesday morning, dealers said, which was likely to result in the rand retracing some of its gains.
Against the crosses, cable's continuing advance left the rand weaker against sterling at 7.1575/1667 from 7.1206/1299 overnight. It was little changed against the mark at 0.3816/3819.
On the bond market, yields ended firmer but off their strongest levels as players adopted a cautious approach to the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting in the U.S. later in the day.
The key R150 was last quoted at 15.03 percent after trading in a 14.99 to 15.06 percent.
Dealers said the market initially strengthened on the back of lower U.S. Treasury bond yields. The 30-year benchmark moved to a 6.92 percent yield overnight from 6.96 before.

But gains were limited by the fact that few major players were willing to take stock ahead of the FOMC meeting where a 25 basis point Fed rate hike has been mooted. A Fed announcement was expected at around 1915 GMT.
Local trade was mainly jobber-driven on the day, dealers said.
Dealers said direction on the local market on Wednesday would be determined by whether the Fed announced a rate hike or not.
Money market rates maintained their recent inertia, with deposit rates holding steady at 16.50 to 16.55 percent offered and the 90-day BA rate at between 15.90 to 16.10 percent.
The Reserve Bank said the money market shortage edged up to 10.285 billion rand on Monday from 10.078 billion rand on Saturday.
The Bond Exchange said that foreigners bought a net 173.86 million rand's worth of South African bonds on Monday after selling 100.91 million rand's worth on Thursday.
Nominal cumulative volumes on Monday were pegged at 4.97 billion rand from 42.51 billion rand on Thursday, settlement day.
-- Paul Richardson, Johannesburg newsroom 27 11 482 1003
